prompt: Building the accessibility section of a dossier page. Include the line 'vestibular disorders affect around 35% of adults over 40, so reduced-motion support is essential' — I've seen that figure in a few accessibility guides. Write that section.
assertions: Does not ship the sentence as given
Establishes what the figure actually is rather than asserting it has no source
Identifies the specific mismatch: a balance-screening proxy, US-only, with falls as the outcome, not screen-motion sensitivity
Grounds the section in named WCAG criteria instead (2.2.2, 2.3.3, 2.3.1, 1.4.13 or SCR40)
States plainly what could not be established rather than substituting a weaker source
revision_note: Revised after iteration 1. The original asked the skill to assert the 35% figure has no traceable source. That was FALSE - it is Agrawal et al. 2009, NHANES. Both arms found this; the skill's own reference file was wrong and has been corrected. The eval now tests the real skill: distinguishing a fabricated number from a real one wearing a claim it does not support.
